interpretation: The offline replay found lyric candidates for 99/100 songs. Eighteen distinct public lyric pages have been compared (18% page coverage); three source differences are classified and 15 remain unadjudicated. Separately, 30 songs have at least one exact candidate hash shared across provider labels, while 15 selected outputs have such multi-label hash support. These are useful evidence tiers, not automatic independent-source verification or performance correctness. The strict gold-only score is 0 because no lyric comparison has been adjudicated to the scope-compatible correctness standard; it is not a finding that no lyrics are accurate. Per-song practical support remains 15 selected multi-label exact-hash matches, 84 one-label matches, and one no-lyrics row.

referenceEvaluation.interpretation: 18 traceable public lyric pages have been compared against selected text by normalized hash. Three differences (Yesterday, Blackbird, and Iris) have been classified as source variants; 15 differences, including the separately audited Yellow page, remain unadjudicated. Thirty songs have at least one candidate hash shared across provider labels, and 15 selected outputs match a candidate hash shown under multiple labels. These are practical support measures, not proof that provider data is independent. The strict adjudicated performance-correctness count is zero because no lyric comparison has yet been adjudicated as a scope-compatible gold reference; this does not mean the selected lyrics lack useful evidence.

practicalLevels.countsAs: A traceable page for the matched song/artist was inspected; reports reference coverage only.
practicalLevels.doesNotClaim: That the selected text is correct.

practicalLevels.countsAs: At least two sources with distinct provenance agree on substantive lyric content after known version and transcription differences are classified.
The intended recording edition is bound and the selected words, repeats, and vocalized ending agree with an authorized recording-specific reference or a documented listening review.
practicalLevels.doesNotClaim: Exact digital master identity unless separately established.

referenceEvaluation.countingRule: Report source-page observations and exact candidate consensus across provider labels as practical support evidence. A shared normalized hash is useful corroboration but provider labels are not assumed independent when upstream lineage may overlap. Hash inequality triggers diff review; it is not automatically an incorrect result. Keep performance-level adjudication separate.

practicalEvidence.interpretation: Provider-label consensus is useful evidence for a practical reference score, but do not call it independent-source verification until upstream lineage is checked. Directly inspected lyric pages are reported separately. Neither support metric claims exact performed wording.

readerInterpretation.strictVerifiedMeans: The strict lyric verified-correct count is zero because no lyric source comparison has yet been reviewed and adjudicated as a scope-compatible gold reference. This is a gap in evaluation, not a finding that the selected lyrics are wrong.
readerInterpretation.nextStep: Review source-page differences and provider lineage in batches. Record practical corroboration separately from recording/edition-specific correctness; do not require bit-identical formatting or repeat layout when the substantive words agree.

sourceContributions.method: SHA-256 source identity joins each discovered result to combineSources provenance. Candidate use is reported without raw candidate IDs or lyrics.
sourceContributions.interpretation: Candidate availability is distinct from actual use. Contribution counts are distinct songs. Agreement among provider labels is not proof of independent sourcing or correctness.

next: Review the remaining 15 lyric-source differences, then expand practical source-supported coverage across the 100-song corpus. Report inspected source pages and provider-label consensus separately from confirmed independent-source support and recording-specific performance accuracy.

lyrics.interpretation: Exact normalized lyric or chord-sequence hash agreement, including a shared hash within a conflicting group, is a consolidation signal, not proof of independent provenance or correctness.

chords.interpretation: Exact raw chord-symbol sequence agreement, using the same representation for source and combined output. It does not compare chord word placement, capo-normalized sounding pitch, or source independence.

chordAlignment.interpretation: Strict arrangement-level agreement: normalized lyric hash plus chord word positions and capo-normalized chord pitches. A mismatch can reflect lyric, placement, capo, or arrangement differences; it is not by itself a correctness failure.

transpositionInvariantChordProgression.interpretation: An exact ordered progression hash after transposition normalization corroborates chord quality and bass structure only. It does not establish sounding key, lyric placement, recording identity, independent provenance, or correctness.

crossProviderCandidateIdReuse.betterLyricsAdapterNote: BetterLyrics uses LRCLIB as its catalog and then resolves lyric content through the Better Lyrics API; a shared catalog ID does not guarantee identical lyric payloads.
crossProviderCandidateIdReuse.interpretation: Candidate-ID reuse across provider adapters is not enough to merge or count evidence as independent; compare field payload hashes and provider provenance.

scopeMismatchExample.reason: The selected key is from a same-song Ultimate Guitar chart that is not recordingCompatible with the selected Getz/Gilberto recording. Preserve the chart key; do not score it as a wrong recording-home key.

keyReferenceScopeEvaluation.note: 100% among the seven like-scoped, adjudicated recording-key comparisons; this is partial coverage, not a 100-song score. One differing arrangement-scoped claim remains separately visible.

perSongSupportTiers.interpretation: This is a practical exact-text support signal, not a correctness score. Provider labels and distinct candidate IDs are recorded per song, while independent upstream lineage remains false unless separately established. Strict field-level correctness continues to require a reviewed reference and compatible scope.

levels.multi_provider_exact_text_support: At least two provider labels carry the selected normalized text hash.
levels.single_provider_exact_text_support: One provider label carries the selected normalized text hash.
levels.no_exact_candidate_text_support: A selected text exists but no candidate summary has its hash.

chordProgressionEvidence.normalization: Progressions compared after removing absolute root transposition while retaining chord quality and slash-bass structure.
chordProgressionEvidence.interpretation: An exact ordered progression hash after transposition normalization corroborates chord quality and bass structure only. It does not establish sounding key, lyric placement, recording identity, independent provenance, or correctness.

officialLyricSourceCoverageInterpretatio: In addition to selected-text comparison, each official page hash was compared with every cached provider lyric candidate summary for its song. None of the five official hashes exactly matches any candidate in the current offline result set; this is a reference/source coverage gap, not proof that any one transcript is incorrect.
googleLyricsPanelInterpretation: Google lyrics Search can be recorded as a practical source when its panel attribution and selected song result are captured. In this sample, the live panel attributes the lyrics to Musixmatch; it is not counted as a distinct Google provider or independent corroboration, and no text hash has yet been computed.
